variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: An episode starts in subgoal A (pick up the cube). Rules, applied to whatever the step shows: Whether the cube is held is decided from the fingers and gripper at the scene of this decision step alone, never from the cube's own line: the cube IS held whenever the fingers are ~46% open (any partly closed value, not ~100%) and the gripper is raised (height above ~0.1), even if the cube line lacks the words 'held in the gripper' or still reports its old table coordinates; the execution steps leading to that scene show the gripper descending to the cube, the fingers closing from ~100% to ~46%, and the gripper rising. The cube is NOT held only when the fingers are ~100% open. 1. If the goal-named cube is NOT held (fingers ~100% open): choose A, pick up the cube, pointing at the current position of the goal-named cube as shown in the scene at this decision step (typically near [82, 127] at the start of execution). This is always the case at the first decision step. 2. If the goal-named cube IS held (fingers ~46% open and gripper raised, by the test above): choose B, drop onto, pointing at the target listed in the scene at this decision step whose position is closest to goal_target from memory, using that target's coordinates exactly as listed in this step's scene rather than the memory value (targets wobble by a few pixels between frames). If goal_target is unknown, apply rule 4. 3. Never choose C (press the button); the button is part of the demonstration only, not of the task. 4. If the situation matches no rule (e.g. the cube is held but goal_target is unknown, or the cube is not visible): if a cube is held, drop onto the target nearest the image centre; otherwise choose A pointing at the goal-named cube's last visible position. After a drop has been completed the episode is over; if asked again, repeat rule 1 or 2 as the scene dictates.

fields.name: goal_target
fields.description: At the first decision step (demonstration frames are shown and the carried memory is empty), follow this procedure and no other: (1) walk the demonstration frames in ascending t. (2) A placement is a frame where the gripper is low (height below ~0.07) and the fingers go from a partly closed value (~45% to ~95%; the low frame itself may read 67%, 80% or 93%) to ~100% open, right after frames in which the goal-named cube was carried (its line read 'held in the gripper' with the gripper raised). (3) Its target is the listed target closest to where the cube rests in the following frames, with coordinates taken from the last demonstration frame, where all four targets are listed. (4) Drop the demonstration's final placement (cube left near [82, 127], no target within ~15 pixels), drop button presses (fingers 0%, no cube carried), and do not count a carried cube that briefly loses its 'held' label while the gripper stays raised. (5) Number what is left 1, 2, 3, 4 earliest first and write the [y, x] of the target of the placement the goal's ordinal names ('first' = 1, 'second' = 2, 'third' = 3, 'fourth' = 4). Count forward from the earliest placement only, never backward from the most recent one; a button press between placements does not restart the count. Example: placements near [99, 90], [100, 163], [141, 133], [79, 90] then the centre set-down; 'second' gives the last-frame coordinates of the second, e.g. [98, 166]; 'first' gives [99, 90]. At every later step copy the carried-in value unchanged. unknown only if no demonstration frames are shown and nothing is carried in. e.g. [139, 124]
fields.annotation: The single target position, in [y, x], on which the goal-named cube (the colour named in the goal instruction) is to be dropped. Written at step #1, the only step that shows the demonstration, and copied unchanged at every later step; unknown before the demonstration has been seen. Fill it by this procedure and no other: (1) walk the demonstration frames in ascending t. (2) A placement is a frame where the gripper is low (height below ~0.07) and the fingers go from a partly closed value (anything between ~45% and ~95%; the low frame itself may read 67%, 80% or 93%) to ~100% open, in the frames right after the goal-named cube was carried (its line read 'held in the gripper' while the gripper was raised). (3) The placement's target is the listed target closest to where the cube then rests, with its coordinates copied from the last demonstration frame, where all four targets are listed. (4) Discard the final placement of the demonstration, the one that leaves the cube near [82, 127] with no target within ~15 pixels; discard button presses (fingers 0%, no cube carried); ignore a carried cube that momentarily loses its 'held' label while the gripper stays raised. (5) Number the remaining placements 1, 2, 3, 4 in the order they occur, earliest = 1, and write the target of the placement whose number the goal's ordinal names ('first' = 1, 'second' = 2, 'third' = 3, 'fourth' = 4). The ordinal always counts forward from the earliest placement, never backward from the most recent one, and a button press between placements does not restart the count. Example: placements in order onto targets near [99, 90], [100, 163], [141, 133], [79, 90], then the centre set-down; goal 'second' gives the last-frame listing of the second one, e.g. [98, 166]; goal 'first' gives [99, 90]. e.g. [139, 124]

initial.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: An episode starts in subgoal A (pick up the cube). Rules, applied to whatever the step shows: 1. If the cube named in the goal instruction is NOT held (fingers ~100% open, gripper raised or empty, cube resting on the table): choose A, pick up the cube, pointing at the current position of the goal-named cube as shown in the scene at this decision step (typically near [82, 127] at the start of execution). This is always the case at the first decision step. 2. If the goal-named cube IS held (fingers ~46% open, gripper raised to height ~0.15, cube listed as held or at the gripper position): choose B, drop onto, pointing at goal_target from memory. If goal_target is unknown but demo_placements is non-empty, point at the entry of demo_placements selected by the ordinal in the goal instruction (first=1, second=2, third=3, fourth=4). 3. Never choose C (press the button); the button is part of the demonstration only, not of the task. 4. If the situation matches no rule (e.g. the cube is held but memory is empty and no list can be derived, or the cube is not visible): if a cube is held, drop onto the target nearest the image centre; otherwise choose A pointing at the goal-named cube's last visible position. After a drop has been completed the episode is over; if asked again, repeat rule 1 or 2 as the scene dictates.

fields.name: demo_placements
fields.description: At the first decision step (the one that shows DEMONSTRATION STEPS and the memory is empty), scan the demo frames for the cube whose colour the goal instruction names, and write the ordered list of target positions, in [y, x], where it was released: a release is a frame where the fingers open from ~46% to ~100% right after frames where that cube was 'held in the gripper'; record the target whose position (read from a demo frame listing all four targets, such as the last demo frame) is closest to where the cube now rests. Skip the demo's final release near the image centre (cube left around [82, 127] with no target there), skip the cube's starting spot, and skip button presses (fingers 0% open, no cube held). At every later step, copy the carried-in value unchanged. Empty list if no demonstration frames are shown and nothing is carried in. e.g. [[116, 163], [75, 163]]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of target positions, in [y, x], on which the goal-named cube (the colour named in the goal instruction) was released during the DEMONSTRATION, in the order the releases happened. A release is a frame where the fingers go from ~46% open to ~100% open while that cube was 'held in the gripper' just before; the entry is the position of the target closest to the cube's resting spot right after that release, taken from a demo frame where all four targets are visible (e.g. the last demo frame). Do NOT include the demo's final release near the image centre (cube left around [82, 127], no target there), do not include the cube's starting spot, do not include button presses, and do not include a release that is onto the same target the cube was just lifted from if no target lies under the cube. Written at step #1 (the only step that shows the demonstration) and copied unchanged at every later step. Empty list only if no demonstration was shown. e.g. [[116, 163], [75, 163]]

fields.name: goal_target
fields.description: At the first decision step, after writing demo_placements, take the ordinal in the goal instruction ('first' = entry 1, 'second' = entry 2, 'third' = entry 3, 'fourth' = entry 4) and write that entry of demo_placements as a [y, x] point. At every later step copy the carried-in value unchanged. unknown if demo_placements is empty. e.g. [116, 163]
fields.annotation: The single target position, in [y, x], that the goal instruction's ordinal picks out of demo_placements: 'first' = entry 1, 'second' = entry 2, 'third' = entry 3, 'fourth' = entry 4. Written at step #1 from the demonstration and copied unchanged afterwards. unknown before the demonstration has been seen. e.g. [116, 163]

the policy prompt for subgoal
  Rule 1 and rule 2 decide 'held' from the cube's label and finger opening, and that sent the policy wrong at the decision step after the pick-up: the scene at that step shows the gripper raised to height ~0.15 with the fingers ~46% open, but the goal-named cube is listed at its old table position without the words 'is held in the gripper', so neither rule matched and the policy chose A again instead of B. Replace the held test in rules 1 and 2 with this: the cube IS held whenever the fingers at the decision step are ~46% open (not ~100%) and the gripper is raised (height above ~0.1), regardless of whether the cube line carries the 'held' label or still reports the old table coordinates; the execution steps leading to that scene will show the gripper descending to the cube, the fingers closing from ~100% to ~46%, and the gripper rising. The cube is NOT held only when the fingers are ~100% open. In that held case choose B, drop onto. Rule 2 should also say where to point: at the target listed in the current scene that is closest to goal_target (targets wobble by a few pixels between frames), and if goal_target is unknown, fall back to rule 4. Rule 2's clause about deriving the point from demo_placements must go, since that field no longer exists. Rules 3 and 4 stand. Rule 1 stands for the first decision step, where the fingers are 100% open and the gripper is raised out of frame.

refused
  Four steps at the drop decision reported that goal_target was wrong and asked that the policy prompt insist on chronological ordering of the demonstration releases (or, in one case, that the memory be checkable against the scene). I am not passing the ordering demand on as a fix, because across this minibatch no single ordering reproduces the recorded drops: in two episodes the recorded target is the ordinal-th release counted earliest first, in two others it is the ordinal-th release counted latest first, and in one the recorded drop is onto a target the demonstration never placed the cube on at all. The reports contradict each other, and a rule written to satisfy one would break another; the chronological definition is kept as the stated rule because it is the plain reading of the goal and fits the cases that fit anything. The request to add a way to 'override' a goal_target in the scene is refused as well: nothing in the execution scene reveals which target the demonstration used, so the memory is the only source and cannot be checked against the step. The only reliable fault across these steps was the held-cube test and the pointing rule, which are passed on above.

One small clarification to rule 2: when choosing B, point at the exact coordinates of the listed target nearest goal_target as they appear in the scene at this decision step; a point one or two pixels off that listing is still correct, since targets wobble, and the recorded points are sometimes one pixel from the listing. refused
  Two reports asked for the counting to be changed so that, in one demonstration with two placements and a button press between them, 'first' resolves to the later placement, and in another with four placements 'second' resolves to the earliest one. These two demands contradict each other (one wants the most recent placement, the other the earliest) and both contradict the three other episodes in the minibatch, where 'first' is confirmed as the earliest placement in demonstrations with two or three placements and a button press at various positions. No single counting rule fits all five recorded drops, so the earliest-first rule, which fits three of five, is kept and only made unambiguous. The report that 'first' should be read backwards from the most recent placement is likewise dropped: it was offered because the annotation at that step had itself been filled backwards, against the rule, and that annotation error is what the rule rewrite corrects. The suggestion that a hidden or covered target identifies the placement is not needed: the target coordinates are to be read from the last demonstration frame, where all four are listed.

refused
  Two steps reported the same thing: at the second decision step, with the goal-named cube just grasped and raised, the policy dropped onto the target that the carried-in goal_target named, and the recorded drop was onto a different target. Both steps concluded that the ordinal procedure in the first-step rule had numbered the placements wrongly and asked for it to be sharpened (re-grasps near the same target, cubes resting between two targets, non-goal-cube placements). Both were second decision steps on a goal naming the 'first' target: the robot had just lifted the goal-named cube from the centre of the table (fingers partly closed, gripper raised), the memory carried goal_target as the target of the earliest demonstration placement, and the policy chose 'drop onto' that target. If the cube named in the goal instruction is NOT held (fingers ~100% open, gripper raised or empty, cube resting on the table): choose A, pick up the cube, pointing at the current position of the goal-named cube as shown in the scene at this decision step (typically near [82, 127] at the start of execution). This is always the case at the first decision step. 2. If the goal-named cube IS held (fingers ~46% open, gripper raised to height ~0.15, cube listed as held or at the gripper position): choose B, drop onto, pointing at goal_target from memory. fields.name: demo_placements
fields.description: At the first decision step (the one that shows DEMONSTRATION STEPS and the memory is empty), scan the demo frames for the cube whose colour the goal instruction names, and write the ordered list of target positions, in [y, x], where it was released: a release is a frame where the fingers open from ~46% to ~100% right after frames where that cube was 'held in the gripper'; record the target whose position (read from a demo frame listing all four targets, such as the last demo frame) is closest to where the cube now rests. Skip the demo's final release near the image centre (cube left around [82, 127] with no target there), skip the cube's starting spot, and skip button presses (fingers 0% open, no cube held). At every later step, copy the carried-in value unchanged. Empty list if no demonstration frames are shown and nothing is carried in. e.g. [[116, 163], [75, 163]]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of target positions, in [y, x], on which the goal-named cube (the colour named in the goal instruction) was released during the DEMONSTRATION, in the order the releases happened. A release is a frame where the fingers go from ~46% open to ~100% open while that cube was 'held in the gripper' just before; the entry is the position of the target closest to the cube's resting spot right after that release, taken from a demo frame where all four targets are visible (e.g. the last demo frame). Do NOT include the demo's final release near the image centre (cube left around [82, 127], no target there), do not include the cube's starting spot, do not include button presses, and do not include a release that is onto the same target the cube was just lifted from if no target lies under the cube.
